prompt: What is prop drilling?
hint: Think of the components in the middle.

choices.text: A bug in which a prop changes on its way down through the tree
choices.why: Props arrive as they were passed; nothing changes them on the way.

choices.text: Passing a value through components that only hand it on
choices.why: Right. It is honest, and noisy when the middle grows props it does not use.

choices.text: Reading a prop from inside an effect
choices.why: That is ordinary, and has nothing to do with depth.

choices.text: Binding a prop through several components with bind:
choices.why: Binding is two-way; drilling is about passing through the middle, one way or the other.

prompt: `Status` reads `total` and `doneMinutes`, `Days` reads `week` and `byDay`. What do the two really need?
hint: It is never a single value.

choices.text: Four separate props, one per field they read, passed from the page
choices.why: That works, and grows by one prop for every new field.

choices.text: The planner itself, the whole instance whose fields they read
choices.why: Right: they read a few of its fields, which change as they change.

choices.text: A copy of the planner's data, taken when they are created
choices.why: A copy would stop following the planner the moment it was taken.

prompt: Which of these make context the right tool? Choose all that apply.
hint: The section lists three conditions.

choices.text: Many components inside one part of the page need the same thing
choices.why: Yes, the first condition.

choices.text: The thing belongs to that part of the page, not to the whole application
choices.why: Yes, the second.

choices.text: The value must be the same for every visitor of the site
choices.why: That describes a module-level constant, not context.

choices.text: Only one component needs it, two levels down
choices.why: One reader is what a prop is for.

prompt: Two `Planner.svelte` components sit side by side on one page. What does a `Days` inside the second one get?
hint: Context goes to a component's own descendants.

choices.text: Whichever planner was set last on the page
choices.why: That would make context a global, which it is not.

choices.text: An error, because a context may only be set once per page
choices.why: Each component may set its own, for its own children.

choices.text: The one its own nearest ancestor set
choices.why: Right. The nearest component above that set it decides.

choices.text: The first planner, since it was created earlier
choices.why: Creation order does not matter; the tree above does.

prompt: What does `createContext()` return?
hint: The lesson destructures it in `context.js`.

choices.text: A key string to pass to `setContext` and `getContext`
choices.why: It replaces keys altogether.

choices.text: A pair of functions, one that gets the value and one that sets it for the components inside
choices.why: Right, and a third that says whether it was set.

choices.text: A store holding the value, read with `$`
choices.why: It is not a store; it hands over a value.

choices.text: A component that wraps the children it provides for
choices.why: It is a pair of functions, not a component.

prompt: Why can `Planner.svelte` write `const planner = setPlanner(new Planner(…))` in one line?
hint: What does the setter give back?

choices.text: `setPlanner` returns the value it was given
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `setPlanner` creates a reactive copy of the instance and returns the copy
choices.why: No copy is made: it is the same instance.

choices.text: Because `new` inside a function call is evaluated after the call returns
choices.why: Arguments are evaluated first, as anywhere in JavaScript.

prompt: How many lines of `Planner.svelte`'s markup did the two tags `<Status />` and `<Days />` replace?
hint: The note in the example says it.

prompt: After ticking the session of the 24th, `Status` and `Days` agree with the rest of the page. Why?
hint: How many planners are there?

choices.text: The context sends them an update event whenever the planner changes
choices.why: A context is not reactive by itself; it handed over the instance once.

choices.text: They read fields of the one planner the page changes
choices.why: Right. One instance, signals in its fields.

choices.text: The page re-creates both components after every change
choices.why: Nothing is re-created; only what read the changed fields updates.

choices.text: Each one keeps its own planner and copies the page's on change
choices.why: There is only one planner, set by the page.

prompt: `createContext` is part of Svelte since version 5.___.
hint: Before it, `setContext` and `getContext` with a key.

prompt: `Days` is rendered on a page with no `Planner.svelte` around it. What happens?
hint: Read the first line of the server's message.

choices.text: It renders an empty list and logs a warning
choices.why: `getPlanner()` throws; nothing is rendered quietly.

choices.text: It creates a planner of its own with no sessions
choices.why: Nothing creates a planner except the code that calls `new Planner`.

choices.text: An error, `missing_context`, and a 500 page
choices.why: Right. The stack names `Days.svelte` as the component that asked.

prompt: Why is the error from `getPlanner()` better than what the older `getContext(key)` did?
hint: What did the old one return?

choices.text: The old one crashed the whole server instead of one page
choices.why: It did the opposite: it returned quietly.

choices.text: The old one returned `undefined` and the failure came later, somewhere less helpful
choices.why: Right. A failure at the point of the mistake is easier to fix.

choices.text: The new one fixes the missing context by itself
choices.why: It reports it; the fix is yours.

choices.text: They behave the same; only the name of the function changed
choices.why: One throws, one returned `undefined`.

prompt: A component should work with or without a planner above it. What does it use?
hint: `createContext` returns three functions.

choices.text: A `try … catch` around every read of a planner field
choices.why: The check belongs before getting, not around every read.

choices.text: The third function: `hasPlanner() ? getPlanner() : null`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `getPlanner(null)`, which returns its argument when nothing was set
choices.why: The getter takes no default; it throws.

prompt: A button's click handler calls `getPlanner()` to add a session. What happens?
hint: When may context be read?

choices.text: It fails: by then Svelte no longer knows which component is asking
choices.why: Right. Get it at the top of the script, keep it in a constant.

choices.text: It works, since the planner the page created is still on the page and still in context
choices.why: Being on the page is not enough; context is read during creation.

choices.text: It returns a fresh planner with the data as it was first loaded
choices.why: Nothing makes a new planner.

prompt: Match what the parent sets with what a child sees later.
hint: Only one keeps following the planner.

pairs.right: The total as it was when set

right_distractors: An error the first time the total changes

prompt: A child needs only the current total. What should the parent put in context?
hint: A function call is read when it runs.

choices.text: `planner.total`, which the child then reads with `$derived`
choices.why: The number was copied when it was set; deriving from a copy follows nothing.

choices.text: A function, `() => planner.total`, which the child calls whenever it needs the total
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A new `$state` variable holding the total, set once
choices.why: Set once, it would never follow the planner's total.

choices.text: The total as a string, since strings are passed by reference
choices.why: Strings are values like numbers; that changes nothing.

prompt: `setContext('total', total)` with a `$state` variable makes the compiler warn `state_referenced____`.
hint: The same warning as lesson 2's `hours`.

prompt: Why will lesson 13 update the planner's fields in place instead of making a new `Planner` when data arrives?
hint: Look at the second row of the table.

choices.text: Creating instances of a class is slow on the server
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: A class with runes can only be constructed once per page
choices.why: Nothing limits how many are made.

choices.text: Children hold the instance they were given, so a new one would never reach them
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Ana opens `/hello?name=Ana`, then a stranger opens `/hello` with the module version. What does the stranger see?
hint: One copy of the module answers both.

choices.text: `Hello, stranger.`
choices.why: That is the context version.

choices.text: `Hello, Ana.`
choices.why: Right: the first request set the name in the module the second request read.

choices.text: An error, since two requests wrote the same object
choices.why: Nothing errors, which is why it is dangerous.

choices.text: An empty greeting until the first request has finished
choices.why: The first had finished; its value stayed.

prompt: Why does a module-level value cause no trouble in the browser?
hint: Who holds the page?

choices.text: The browser holds one page for one person
choices.why: Right, so the value is that person's.

choices.text: Browsers copy every module once per component that imports it
choices.why: A module is loaded once per page, in the browser too.

choices.text: Svelte resets module state on every client-side navigation
choices.why: It keeps it, as the timer of lesson 10 did.

prompt: Put the fix for the greeting in order.
hint: The module changes first; the page uses what it exports.
items: The module exports `createContext()`'s pair instead of an instance
The page creates its own `$state` visitor from the address
Each request greets its own visitor
trap: Setting a context needs the value to exist first.

prompt: Which of these is safe at module level on a page rendered on the server?
hint: Is it the same for everybody?

choices.text: The selected course of the student who is browsing
choices.why: That belongs to one person.

choices.text: A list of sessions loaded for the current visitor
choices.why: Private to one visitor: it would leak to the next.

choices.text: A function that formats dates for display
choices.why: Right: the same for everybody.

choices.text: The name typed into a form by the last person who submitted it
choices.why: Exactly the leak the section shows.

prompt: A theme setting chosen by each visitor must reach twenty components across the layout. Where does it go?
hint: Per visitor, many readers, rendered on the server.

choices.text: An exported `$state` object in a `.svelte.js` module
choices.why: On the server it would be shared between visitors.

choices.text: An object in context, set by the component that holds them all
choices.why: Right: one per request, reachable at any depth.

choices.text: A prop passed by hand through every component in between
choices.why: It works, at the price the first section described.

prompt: Match each value with where it belongs.
hint: Who does it belong to, and who reads it?

pairs.left: The planner, read by Status and Days

right_distractors: A module-level `$state` shared by every request
